regions.full_page: I received your pathietic letter of January 23rd and do surely sympathise with you. I hope, however, that is His great mercy and in- finite wisdom the good God may see fit to draw good from your plight and as He never fails to do, inasmuch as we take our crosses in resig- nation at least to His holy will, turn your seeming misfortune to have been a blessing in disguise. I have been down here in St. Felix since last April. So for the present am no more at St. Bonaverture's in Detroit; though I was up in Detroit all last week, as the little cards may at least intimate. You might do well, nevertheless to visit the Monastery there on Mt. Elliott (#1740). They can enroll you in the Seraphic Mass Associa- tion as well as I can, and that is a big feature in the "secret" of the many notable favors there reported - as well as in our other friaries. Thanks be to God. At all events, dear Mr. Taylor, I am going to tell you of just one of said notables; that you may draw your own conclusion and as I sincerely hope, draw therefrom a happily profitable lesson. The case was noted close to four years ago in my own hand and runs sub- stantially as follows: "March 26th, 1943, Andrew Wheeler, a methodest of 686 Manistique Ave., Detroit, had 'brain-tumor' removed four weeks ago, (Febr. 23). At first, operation seemed to have been successful but two weeks later infection started. March 12th second operation. "Last Tuesday, March 23rd Mrs. Wheeler accompanied by a Catholic neighbor came weepingly lamenting; " ... They have just operatid on my Husband the third time in a month and they give me very little hope of his recovery. .. " "Now Mrs. Wheeler", I pleaded, "do not take it so hard. We will pray for your husband and enroll him in the Mass Association and try to in- duce the our dear Lord to take over the case Himself". .... I re- corded Mr. W's name, etc.

regions.full_page: God bless you and your poorly, dear Wife, Bernice. May He bless your whole family and all your friends!
